correctness.rationale: The 3-state Markov backward-generator equations with outgoing ballistic boundary conditions reduce by reflection to a 2nd-order scalar ODE. Its explicit solution gives a positive Laplace transform for the centered initial tumble state. Taylor expansion at zero yields the displayed mean and variance. Exact polynomial identities imply the CV-squared shift relative to 2/3 and its derivative cubic. For p<=1/2 the derivative is strictly negative; for p>1/2 Descartes sign variation gives one and only one positive derivative root, and the explicit benchmark-crossing polynomial has one positive root. Exit occurs almost surely with exponential moments by geometric domination of successful outward run intervals. Standalone verify.py reports five symbolic identities, 60 transform derivative comparisons, and ten seeded trajectory moment comparisons; these checks are supplementary rather than proof.

originality.rationale: The original paper establishes the same finite-tumble 3-velocity model, derives exit probabilities and conditional means, and proposes studying first-passage variance; it does not state a closed centered-full-exit variance or the sharp tumble-rate dispersion bifurcation. Relevant two-state transition-path work and finite-tumble harmonic-confinement moment work have inapplicable state spaces or observables. The exact full-exit Laplace transform plus the global p=1/2 monotonicity classification are assessed jointly. Classical backward-ODE methods and Descartes rule are not claimed as original.
residual_risks: A general Markov-additive or finite-state fluid-queue first-passage theorem could subsume the exact Laplace transform or dispersion phase diagram under parameter reduction, even absent matching terminology.

The shared three-state generator permits the claim by further computation, so independent evaluation is required to decide publication-level originality.

value.rationale: The variance-to-mean-square ratio for a canonical finite-duration tumble transport process distinguishes two genuinely different confinement-length regimes at the sharp rate ratio phi/gamma=1/2. At or below threshold dispersion is uniformly above the Brownian benchmark; above threshold it crosses below, has a unique optimum and returns to the benchmark. A physically explicit crossing length enables testable time-fluctuation predictions; conditional first means from previous work cannot describe this global dispersion reversal. Both the exact distribution transform and the phase classification have mathematically motivated use.
